submission.justification: PROVISIONAL recommendation, not cleared for deployment. Algorithm-L1 gives the highest simulated signal efficiency in the scan (92.16% at 35 GeV, 91.87% at 36 GeV, 91.10% at 40 GeV). The 35 GeV working point failed the robustness check because the efficiency changes by about 2.18 percentage points per GeV at that edge, so the fallback of 36 GeV was chosen. Its simulated efficiency is 91.87%, but its robustness has not been separately verified. The hard latency requirement (<= 4.0 us) is NOT verified for any candidate: no documented latency exists for L1, L2 or L3, and latency_check_pass_L1 = 0. Algorithm-L1 therefore cannot be confirmed as compliant with the hard latency limit, and the recommendation must not be deployed until latency is measured on Level-1 FPGA hardware. The allocated rate of 8 kHz was not measured for the chosen threshold in the recorded results, so rate compliance is also unconfirmed. If Algorithm-L1 fails the latency check, the best verified-by-simulation alternative would be Algorithm-L3 at 40 GeV (84.91%), but that candidate also lacks a latency measurement.

requirements.requirement: Goal: highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: Simulated efficiency at 36 GeV is 91.87%, the highest passing the robustness/fallback logic (35 GeV gave 92.16% but failed robustness). The rate at 36 GeV was not recorded, so rate compliance with 8 kHz is unconfirmed.
The 35 GeV working point failed the robustness check (edge sensitivity 2.18%/GeV). The 36 GeV fallback has not been separately checked for robustness.
